messages:
alex.w: Heads-up — we've had 3 customer escalations this week about 429s and long tail latency when customers hit bursty traffic. Need to run a focused load test to pick sane RPM/TPM defaults + burst window.

maria.g: Agreed. Do we have current default values? I think hosted uses 60 rpm / 120 tpm with 30s burst window? Not sure.

jamie.s: Hosted defaults are 100 RPM, 500 TPM in prod config, but Dedicated has overrides. 😕

dong: For context, the problematic customers had short-lived spikes ~200r/s for 10-30s. We saw token-level queues spike and 429s because of token bucket refill mismatch.

alex.w: Plan: 1) run microbench to replay realistic spike shapes (ramp, square, sawtooth) 2) measure 95/99p latency and 429 rate 3) vary RPM/TPM and burst window/sec. Can someone draft k6/vegeta script?

jamie.s: I'll drop a vegeta recipe. Using vegeta for short spikes is easiest. Example we used yesterday:

```bash
echo 'GET https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate' > targets.txt
cat targets.txt | vegeta attack -rate=200 -duration=30s | vegeta report
```

maria.g: Add header for api-key and variable prompt size. We should also run with different concurrency to emulate multiple API keys hitting same route.

alex.w: Notes: include cold-start trials for larger models (context length 4k) and a quantized small model. Also run with backend-sim on to avoid billing churn.

dong: I ran a quick synthetic earlier — with rate=200/30s we saw 4% 429 and p99 token latency 1.6s. Increasing burst window to 60s dropped 429 to 0.6% but increased p99 to 2.4s.

support-bot: ticket #CS-9142 updated: customer attached sample logs and timestamps.

jamie.s: Suggest matrix: RPM {50,100,200}, TPM {300,600,1200}, burst window {15s,30s,60s}. Run 3 seeds each. Collect 429 rate, p95/p99 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, queue length.

maria.g: Can we also capture per-api-key aggregation? If one key spikes it should be isolated; if many keys spike simultaneous we need global guardrails.

alex.w: Assignments: jamie to run vegeta experiments on staging cluster today; dong to instrument queue depth and token-bucket logs; maria to collate metrics and build the summary table. I'll own thresholds proposal.

ops-oncall: FYI — I'll temporarily raise dedicated burst cap for a repro window if needed. Ping me before you start so I can watch.

alex.w: Timeline: run tests by EOD, sync 11:30am tomorrow. If results show >1% 429 at customer-realistic spikes, propose raising default TPM or widening burst window. Otherwise tighten to avoid abuse.

maria.g: Added checklist: include curl repro steps, capture HTTP headers X-RateLimit-*, and attach raw vegeta output. :white_check_mark:

jamie.s: Starting run in 5m. Will post logs back here. :rocket:

alex.w: Thanks — post the raw JSON outputs here and I'll draft the PR for default changes.
